Space is a vacuum and sound waves can’t travel through it in the same way they do on Earth, meaning you wouldn't be able to hear anything in space. But space isn’t entirely silent. Electromagnetic vibrations, like plasma waves or magnetic field interactions, can be translated into sound by instruments. NASA has even 'sonified' data from planets, stars, black holes and nebulae, turning invisible cosmic phenomena into eerie soundtracks. You can hear what this sounds like in the video above. plan.title: 5 Weird Facts About Space
plan.description: Five strange facts about space, from a planet that would float to a day longer than a year. A quick tour of the oddities in our solar system and beyond.

beats.narration: Imagine a planet so light it could float in a bathtub. Space is full of facts that sound made up, but are real. Here are five. Number one: Saturn is less dense than water.

Number two: Mercury has a day longer than its year. It circles the Sun in 88 Earth days, but sunrise to sunrise takes 176. Number three: the hottest planet is Venus, not Mercury, thanks to its thick atmosphere.

props.title: Mercury: year vs sunrise to sunrise

beats.narration: Number four: a single teaspoon of neutron star weighs as much as all the humans on Earth combined. These stars can also spin 600 times every second. Number five: space is silent, because sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

accuracy.reason: The facts match the notes, but "a teaspoon of neutron star weighs as much as all the humans" is a shaky claim, and "Mercury has a day longer than its year" is true only for the solar day, which the script half-explains. Saturn is stated flatly, and "can spin 600 times" is hedged properly.

coverage.reason: It delivers five facts, but they are mostly well-known ones. Beat 2 packs two facts into one beat and the Mercury explanation is thin. The bonus sonification fact is a nice touch.

structure.reason: The numbered list is clear, but the pacing is uneven: beat 2 carries two facts while beat 1 carries one. Fact 5 (silence) is then contradicted by the closing sonification, which muddies the takeaway.

hook_ending.reason: "Imagine a planet so light it could float in a bathtub" is a decent hook. The ending, "stranger than fiction... look up tonight", is a cliché.

tone.reason: The tone is casual, brisk and suitable for a general audience.

visuals.reason: The bar_race for Mercury has identical values across every period, so it is a meaningless animation and misuses the chart. The bullets in beat 3 repeat the narration, and no scene shows Venus.

originality.reason: These are the standard stock space facts, and the closing line is a cliché.

instructions.reason: It gives five facts in about 1 minute, in English, close to the word target.

language.reason: The grammar is fluent. Minor awkwardness remains in "facts that sound made up, but are real".

defects.issue: The bar_race has constant values over time, so it conveys no race or change. A simple static comparison would do.
